 Andhra Pradesh Cyclone Akvan to make landfall on Nov 20 along Andhra-Odisha coast 
 The severe cyclone Akvan is expected to cross the coast between Narsapuram in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha on November 20, bringing heavy rains to north Andhra districts. 
 Representative image PTI Written by: TNM Staff Published on :  19 Nov 2026, 5:10 am 
 Copied 
 The severe cyclone Akvan in the west-central Bay of Bengal is likely to make landfall on the afternoon of Friday, November 20 near Gopalpur in Odisha, between Narsapuram in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha. 
 The cyclone has been moving at a speed of 12 kmph over the last six hours, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said in an update issued at 8.45 am on November 19.
 At the time, the cyclone was located 440 km from Narsapur, 440 km from Kalingapatnam, 580 km from Chennai, 530 km from Gopalpur and 590 km from Puri, according to the agency. 
 Under its influence, scattered heavy rains are expected in the north Andhra districts on November 19 and 20. Moderate rainfall is expected in some areas of the north Andhra districts on November 19.
 Wind speeds along the coast are predicted to reach 60-70 kmph, with gusts up to 80 kmph.
 Residents of the north Andhra districts have been asked to remain alert and fishermen were advised not to venture out to sea. 
 This is the third cyclone to affect the coastal Andhra region in less than a month, after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. 
 Cyclone Arnab made landfall on October 28 along the state’s coast, killing at least seven people. A preliminary estimate said the losses caused by the cyclone neared Rs 4,600 crore, including damage to crops and infrastructure. Teams from the Union government had visited the state to carry out a detailed assessment. 
 Within a week, on November 3, Cyclone Murasu made landfall, killing at least eight people – five in Bapatla district, two in Guntur district and one in Palnadu district. According to a preliminary damage assessment, the cyclone caused an estimated loss of Rs 1,918.55 crore to the state. Agricultural crops were estimated to have been damaged across 1,43,122 hectares, affecting 1,86,063 farmers.
